titlePlain: Deciding Which Cloud a New Workload
subtitle: Lesson 4 · Multi-Cloud Cost and Governance

eyebrow: A fixed order, not a fresh debate

steps.label: 1. Compliance / data residency
steps.sub: Non-negotiable — eliminates options before cost even matters

steps.label: 2. Required services exist?
steps.sub: A yes/no filter: can it even run on this candidate at all

steps.label: 3. Skill and real cost
steps.sub: Deciding factors only among what survives steps 1 and 2

code:
New workload needs: a specific managed
AI platform capability

Azure: has the capability   -> stays in
AWS:   no equivalent exists -> eliminated
On-prem: not applicable      -> eliminated

If it were built from containers + object
storage instead, all three would still
be in play after this step.
caption: Required-services is a filter, not a score — a missing service ends the conversation for that candidate.

eyebrow: The default that should win most of the time

steps.label: Default: same cloud as similar workloads
steps.sub: Lowest operational risk, team already runs it well

steps.label: Use effective cost, not list price
steps.sub: Existing commitments and discounts change the real number

steps.label: Multi-cloud = a named exception
steps.sub: Chosen for a specific reason, never a default habit
